standard_prerequisites.name: fpqc descent of quasi-coherent modules
standard_prerequisites.statement: Quasi-coherent modules on algebraic spaces satisfy fpqc descent: compatible descent data descend uniquely (Descent on Spaces, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the whole of part (1) at source lines 1549-1564.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sheaves as descent data for a covering of the final object
standard_prerequisites.statement: If a covering of the final object is given, the category of sheaves is equivalent to the category of descent data for that covering (Sites, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: It makes parts (2)-(7) local on X at source lines 1568-1576.

standard_prerequisites.name: Equivalence of ringed topoi for schemes versus spaces
standard_prerequisites.statement: The embeddings of the etale (and fppf) sites of schemes into those of spaces determine equivalences of ringed topoi (the author's lemma-compare-cohomology-other-topologies, retained as context).
standard_prerequisites.use: It transfers the scheme case to the general case at source lines 1583-1588.

standard_prerequisites.name: The scheme case and intrinsicness of quasi-coherence
standard_prerequisites.statement: The corresponding seven-part statement for schemes (Etale Cohomology, declared as a tagged source pointer) and the fact that quasi-coherence is an intrinsic property of modules, so it transports along the equivalence (Modules on Sites, declared as a tagged source pointer).
standard_prerequisites.use: They finish the proof at source lines 1589-1594.

core_obligations: Part (1): reinterpret compatible sections of f_i^*g^*F as compatible maps O_{U_i} -> f_i^*g^*F with descent data, then descend them by fpqc descent of quasi-coherent modules (source lines 1549-1564).

Locality: choose an etale covering of X by schemes, observe that it covers the final object in each of the three sites so sheaves are descent data, and conclude that each of parts (2)-(7) is local on X (source lines 1566-1580).
Scheme case: for X a scheme use the equivalences of ringed topoi, the scheme statement, and the intrinsicness of quasi-coherence to obtain parts (2)-(7) in general (source lines 1582-1595).

proof_roadmap.step: Part (1) by fpqc descent of quasi-coherent modules, via compatible maps and descent data.
Reduce parts (2)-(7) to X a scheme by locality of the seven properties over an etale covering by schemes.
Apply the ringed-topos equivalences and the scheme case, transporting quasi-coherence by its intrinsicness.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-review-quasi-coherent at source lines 1519-1546, a seven-part statement: the presheaf F^a(Y) = Gamma(Y, f^*F) satisfies the fpqc (hence fppf and etale) sheaf condition; F^a = pi_X^*F on the big etale site and F^a = a_X^*F on the big fppf site; F -> F^a is an equivalence between quasi-coherent O_X-modules and quasi-coherent modules on the big etale (resp. fppf) site; and the identities epsilon_{X,*}a_X^*F = pi_X^*F, a_{X,*}a_X^*F = F and the vanishing of both higher direct images. The author's proof at source lines 1548-1596 proves part (1) by fppc descent of quasi-coherent modules: turning compatible sections into compatible maps O_U -> g^*F and descending them (a cross-chapter proposition declared as a pointer); then reduces parts (2)-(7) to the case of a scheme by choosing an etale covering by schemes, observing that the covering is a covering of the final object in each of the three sites so that sheaves are descent data (a cross-chapter glueing lemma), noting that each of the seven properties is local, and finishing with the equivalences of ringed topoi for a scheme (the author's lemma-compare-cohomology-other-topologies, retained as context) and the scheme case (a cross-chapter pointer), using that being quasi-coherent is intrinsic (another pointer). The author closes with the remark 'Some minor details omitted.'; that remark is reproduced verbatim and the card adds nothing in its place.
